note: Rewrite each summand as a count of binary strings of length 2k+1 whose (k+1)-st 1 occurs at position k+j+1: choose the preceding j zeros among k+j places, then choose the remaining k-j bits freely. Summing j=0,...,k counts precisely strings with a strict majority of 1s. Bitwise complementation bijects these with strict-majority-0 strings; odd length excludes ties, so each class has half of 2^(2k+1), namely 4^k.
